highlights.title: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
highlights.summary: When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games.
body: “I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it’s for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.”

The simulation, titled Exploring Geopolitical Tipping Points and Climate Cooling Strategies, saw a couple dozen foreign-relations experts, scientists, military personnel, and former government officials from across the world convene in a meeting room at Queen Mary University of London. After making introductions over coffee and little yogurts, they sat at tables arranged in a square with the name of the country or organization each person was playing: national governments, climate NGOs and nonprofits, indigenous groups, and tech companies. Golja was assigned to provide technical advice to help participants make scientifically literate decisions.

The world is going to have to make decisions about how to govern this technology much sooner than most policymakers imagine, Cynthia Scharf, a former UN advisor, told WIRED. “It’s not 15 years from now; it’s in the next decade, easily.”

highlights.title: DLSS 5 gets toned down for its Hogwarts Legacy debut next month
highlights.summary: When Nvidia originally showed off DLSS 5 earlier this year, the technology immediately got branded as gen AI for video games. To gamers, Nvidia had lost the plot. I personally couldn't get over how faces were transformed using DLSS 5.
body: DLSS 5 debuts in Hogwarts Legacy and Where Winds Meet next month.

Now more than six months later, DLSS 5 is about to debut properly in Hogwarts Legacy, and it looks like it has been seriously toned down. Nvidia published new comparison screenshots today, where the changes to faces are as subtle as they are in NBA 2K27. Teenagers no longer look like middle-aged men, and even the environmental changes look more subtle.

Nvidia has always maintained that developers have “detailed artistic control” over DLSS 5, and ultimately make the choice on how to implement the technology in their own games. DLSS 5 will now appear in Hogwarts Legacy on November 5th, and it’s also coming to Where Winds Meet late next month.

highlights.title: The Wordle of Pokémon Games Is Here With Daily Challenge Battles
highlights.summary: Do you know Wordle, the word puzzle that challenges you once a day? What if, instead of a puzzle, it were a Pokémon battle? That's the concept of Daily Red, a fan-made Pokémon game that you can play in your browser.
body: In Daily Red, players must face Red daily using a team of six random Pokémon from Gens 1-3. Red leads with Pikachu and always has the same team as when players find him on Mt. Silver in Johto: Pikachu, Espeon, Snorlax, Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise. This allows players to become increasingly acquainted with the lineup over time.

Before battling, gamers are advised to analyze their team for the day. This way, they can understand its strengths and weaknesses and decide which Pokémon to lead with. They can also try a practice run before they commit to the battle. After the battle, they can continue practicing, but their result will be locked in.

The objective is to beat Red and start a winning streak. Unfortunately, it's not currently possible to make an account to save progress, but it's stored locally in the browser. Once the battle is over, players can share their grid with friends or on social media. If they lose, the grid will have red squares, revealing how many of Red's Pokémon fainted. If they win, the grid will have a green square for each of their Pokémon that didn't faint.

highlights.summary: Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, which is now delayed from its original March release window, according to a report from Bloomberg.
body: Developers working on the unannounced shooter game were told to use AI tools like Anthropic’s Claude.

According to Bloomberg, one of the game’s directors said in a message to staff, “No more hand-written code.” Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.” In a statement given to Bloomberg, Epic Games spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI-accelerated development.”
Epic Games and Disney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The upcoming game is reportedly a shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars. It’s part of a multiyear collaboration between Epic and Disney, which also invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024. Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader. But it sounds like Epic may be aiming to have AI do most of the heavy lifting on its new Disney game.

body: Hull City, Ipswich Town and Coventry City are all clear of the Premier League relegation zone after six games; does this put a supposedly safe mid-table club or a big-name team in genuine danger of relegation to the Championship this season?

The Premier League's newly-promoted sides have often struggled to bridge the gap, with two consecutive seasons in 2023/24 and 2024/25 seeing all three newcomers relegated before Leeds and Sunderland helped buck that trend last season.
The lesson teams are learning is that survival is possible when a promoted team gets their recruitment, organisation and mentality right.
Hull and Ipswich already have nine points, while Coventry, following their 4-1 hammering of Newcastle, are on six.

highlights.title: Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home
highlights.summary: It's finally here: Apple's long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it's gorgeous.
body: As Apple debuts Siri AI in the home, it’s focusing on a beautiful, multipurpose screen (and hiding your text messages from your kids), rather than innovative new smart home features.

The HomeView is the centerpiece of Apple’s new push into the home. It costs $299 and launches alongside a new collection of cameras, thermostats, and a door lock designed for Apple Home. As a smart home hub, Matter controller, and Thread Border Router, the HomeView can orchestrate these and other Apple Home and Matter smart home devices. It’s available in eight countries at launch: the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and India. Preorders are open now, with devices shipping November 13th.

The new smart display has Siri AI built in, enabling natural-language voice interactions to ask general knowledge questions, control smart home devices via voice and touch, and get information using personal context from your text messages, calendar, and emails. Personal context requires facial recognition and for your Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone to be on the same network, so your kids can’t peek at your texts over breakfast.

highlights.title: 'Ruins and Reverberations' quest walkthrough in Arc Raiders
highlights.summary: The "Ruins and Reverberations" quest in Arc Raiders involves a quick visit to the Cielo Sereno Observatory, which is one of the new locations on the Pendola Pass map, introduced to the game with the "Frozen Trail" update.
body: Here's a full walkthrough on how to complete the "Ruins and Reverberations" quest in Arc Raiders, including how to get a Spotter Relay and where to find the antenna and the crawlspace under the control room.

First up, you need to get your hands on a Spotter Relay. Spotters, not to be confused with Snitches, are small, flying Arc enemies that always come in pairs. Two of them always deploy alongside a Bastion or Bombardier, and they do exactly what you'd expect: spot raiders. Bastions and Bombardiers aren't often seen on Pendola Pass, so your best bet is to go to Buried City or Blue Gate. Take down a Spotter, loot it for the Spotter Relay, then bring it to Pendola Pass with you.

The Cielo Sereno Observatory is located in the northeast area of Pendola Pass. The antenna itself is on the roof, and you should absolutely bring a grappling hook, snaphook, or zipline with you to do this quest, because you're going to need to get onto the roof of the observatory twice. Having one of these mobility tools on you will make this task considerably easier.

highlights.summary: Composer Hildur Guðnadóttir, who won an Oscar with “Joker,” is already deep into “The Bell Jar.” Sarah Polley’s Sylvia Plath adaptation, which recently wrapped, will give pop icon Billie Eilish her first starring role, while offering the composer a new kind of creative partnership.
body: Composer Hildur Guðnadóttir, who won an Oscar with “Joker,” is already deep into “ The Bell Jar.”

“We talked about what we envisioned for the music, and how we could translate what Sylvia experiences into it,” Guðnadóttir says. “For me, the core of Plath’s writing is that she’s searching for identity. She keeps asking, ‘Who am I?’ and then uses her writing to understand that. Billie, Sarah and I have been exploring how we hear that, how to translate it into music, and what music Sylvia herself might have been listening to.”

“It’s one of the most exciting projects I’ve ever done,” she says. “Sarah and I are good friends, so getting to tell this story with her is amazing. I think it’s one of the most amazing books ever written.”

highlights.title: Companies rushed in on AI. Now some are pulling back
highlights.summary: Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work. Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools.
body: Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents after the company found employees were spending more and more time cleaning up technical and security errors, Reuters reported. And after thinning its workforce, especially middle managers, in a 2023 efficiency push, the company is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show.

At Microsoft, which rolled out AI widely internally, executive vice-president Ryan Roslansky recently publicly lamented the prevalence of AI slop in his day-to-day work. After receiving “what was clearly an AI-generated doc” from a co-worker, he used his AI to summarize it and came away with no new thinking about the idea, he said. He warned his followers against falling into this potential “doom loop”, where AI does the reading and writing and leaves behind an “ocean of sameness”.

Meanwhile, Walmart store and warehouse employees are being plagued by unreasonable expectations, errors and false alerts from AI tools that assign tasks, schedules and monitor performance, Business Insider reported.
points: Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work.
Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools.

highlights.title: Wikipedians Believed AI Would Come and Go. They Were Wrong
highlights.summary: In a world of AI Overviews, Wikipedia usage declines. But the real loss may be far more existential than website traffic.
body: At first, Wikipedians tried to shape and control AI, to make its output “acceptable and constructive,” or to fix or remove if it proved otherwise. Generic fluff like “praising a village for its fertile farmlands, livestock, and scenic countryside” and fake sources were weeded out. By March 2026, AI content was found to violate its core principles so often that writing with large language models was banned outright, and their role restricted to translation and minor proofreading.

Once Google introduced AI Overviews in search, they quickly became as central to the experience as Wikipedia was until recently. (This also means Wikipedia still does play a crucial role as a source, only at one step removed.) Anyone who uses AI agents knows that they give plausible, almost intuitive answers, which can pass a superficial review of their sourcing. They are also often wrong. If Wikipedia itself becomes corrupted by artificial intelligence, by what means will we prove when they are wrong?
points: In a world of AI Overviews, Wikipedia usage declines.

highlights.title: Live-Action Moana Officially Gets Disney Plus Release Date
highlights.summary: Disney ’s latest box office dud is headed for streaming. A little over three months after the live-action film Moana debuted in theaters to an underwhelming box office performance, the movie is coming to Disney Plus on Oct. 21.
body: Moana opened to a dismal $43 million at the domestic box office on opening weekend, a huge whiff considering the movie's $250 million budget. While it eventually made around $323.6 million worldwide, movies typically need to earn double or 2.5 times their budget for the studio to break even, so this was almost certainly a big underperformance for Disney.

Critics blasted the film for failing to find its own identity compared to the 2016 animated movie, and audiences seemed similarly unenthusiastic about a live-action remake of a picture that came out just a decade ago. At least with most of Disney’s other bland live-action retreads, the animated movies they revisited were often decades old.

The original animated Moana and its 2024 sequel are beloved musicals centered on Polynesian culture. Both were huge hits with audiences. The first film has a 96% on Rotten Tomatoes and made $687.2 million on a $150-175 million budget. While its 2024 sequel, Moana 2, was far more divisive among critics, it was an even bigger box office hit, making over $1 billion on a $150 million budget. Both movies are a firm reminder that audiences are eager for good films centered on diverse cultures.

highlights.title: The secret to a non-cloudy chicken stock | Kitchen aide
highlights.summary: Don’t cook it too quickly – and skim, skim, skim, says our expert culinary panel. Why is my chicken stock always cloudy? Ryan, by email From broths and risottos to sauces and braises, there’s no question that a good, flavourful stock will stand you in good stead.
body: Ryan’s clarity issue, Byatt says, is “only ever caused by cooking the stock too quickly or by allowing the fat to boil back into the base liquid”. So it’s crucial to take things low and slow. You will also need a pan that’s “big and heavy enough to give the bones enough room for movement, as well as a very fine sieve for straining the stock”.

On to the actual making, and Alissa Timoshkina, author of Lozhka, goes in cold. She puts chicken legs, drumsticks or a leftover roast chicken carcass in a large pot, adds her stock veg – onions, carrots, celery, garlic, say – and aromats (bay, parsley stalks, peppercorns, for instance), then covers the lot with cold water and brings everything very slowly to a boil. She then turns down the heat and leaves it to cook on a very gentle simmer. In the event of that carefully made stock going a bit cloudy, Timoshkina would seek to mollify that by straining the lot through a fine sieve and stirring in a tablespoon of lemon juice, which has the added benefit of being “great for flavour, too”.

highlights.summary: Character.AI, one of the first breakout startups of the generative AI boom, has filed for bankruptcy and is selling some of its assets to Disney. The company, which builds various online bots for users to chat or roleplay with, has faced mounting scrutiny and lawsuits over the safety of its…
body: The chatbot startup is looking to sell its assets to Disney after years of legal challenges and safety concerns.

In a press release and blog post published Monday, Character said it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US to facilitate the sale of the company and its assets. “Over the past year, we’ve taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve our business amid significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds,” the company said.

In its bankruptcy filing, Character listed estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million. As part of the proposed sale, Disney would serve as the lead bidder for Character.AI’s assets, setting a baseline for competing offers. Disney would pay $20 million for certain undisclosed assets, and provide transition support “using former Company employees it has hired.” It would also receive a nonexclusive license to unspecified intellectual property.

body: Grand Theft Auto 6 will reportedly be released on Windows PC early next year, a new report claims.

On Tuesday, GamesBeat reported GTA 6 will land on PC "within the first three months of 2027." That's according to "four industry sources familiar with the studio’s plans" who anonymously spoke with GamesBeat. Rockstar has not officially commented on its potential plans to bring GTA 6 to PC.

GTA 6 is slated for a Nov. 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. Rockstar famously keeps PC gamers waiting as it prioritizes console launches first for its games. Grand Theft Auto 5 came out in September 2013 for consoles and took over a year and a half to arrive on PC in April 2015, for example. Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar's last brand-new single-player game, took a a year to be released on PC after its console launch.

If GTA 6 does end on PC during the first quarter of 2027, it would mean PC players would only have to wait a few months extra to get their hands on what is shaping up to be the biggest game of the generation.

highlights.title: Yes, Britain’s railways are a mess. But is anyone sober enough to care? | Zoe Williams
highlights.summary: Prosecco for the birthday party, Pimm’s for the horsey bunch, some cheeky Stellas for the short-haul crowd: it was all going down on my train the other morning. On Saturday I went to Liverpool with my youngest, and the overhead lines went down at Crewe, but also there were crew shortages across the…
body: Between Rugby and Birmingham New Street, there was an incredibly festive crowd going to the Horse of the Year show, squishing real fruit into cans of Pimm’s, because it was breakfast time, and also because it was funny. But what were the horses going to make of all this? Because they’re quite short on appreciation for ludic pranking, and famously easy to frighten.

Between Wolverhampton and Stafford, it’s only 13 minutes, so I was mainly awed by how many people could even be bothered to open a can of Stella. Stafford to Liverpool was a stag do, and it was brunch o’clock by now, so running up and down the carriage, yelling “Ay ay ay” in a fake scouse accent, dressed in a Brazilian flag, all fell under the umbrella “having a normal one”.
I abhor British exceptionalism, except on this one subject: exceptionally bad train network; exceptionally fun trains. Would recommend.

highlights.title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
highlights.summary: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk.
body: These days, much of the debate about how to handle open models is playing out in public—and there’s a lot of money resting on its outcome. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has a lot to gain if people continue buying their own hardware to run open models, advocates enthusiastically for the United States to develop more of them, whereas Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who runs a company that could be undermined by cheap, powerful models, advocates for a more cautious approach. But beneath all these commercial incentives, there is real substance to disagreements about open models.

“I think a lot of the way you come down on the openness debate is influenced by how you come down on the AI debate,” says David Gray Widder, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin School of Information. Those who are concerned about AI safety warn that open models can easily be misused by bad actors, whereas those who focus more on AI’s practical potential urge that this power should not sit behind the closed doors of just a few big companies, and that open models could help spread it more widely.

He was asked whether the performance was down to the team being brought closer together by the guilty verdict.

“It probably has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me as it’s more complicated,” he said, “because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan and you are a City fan, I can tell you: ‘Hey, my friend, you cheat’ – or this kind of thing. But we were happy at the end of the game and inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield.”

City, who have appealed against the independent commission’s ruling and continue to protest their innocence, have drawn criticism for the exuberant manner of Sunday’s celebration. Maresca defended the revelry but is conscious of the need to focus on Wednesday’s visit of Paris Saint-Germain in their second Champions League game of the season, following their 2-0 victory at Porto.

highlights.title: Xbox Is Testing A New Streak Feature That Could Make Gaming Feel (More) Like A Chore
highlights.summary: It looks like another new Xbox feature is in development, and this time, it's designed to encourage users to go on a hot streak--of using their console, not disrupting a sports event with a quick birthday-suit-run.
body: Spotted by Game File's Stephen Totilo, a new number appears to be popping up on the dashboard of Xbox users who are signed up for the Xbox Insider program, suggesting that a streak counter is in development. Microsoft hasn't formally announced this feature yet, and it looks like it kicks in after using your Xbox for three days in a row per week. It's an idea that Microsoft has experimented with in the past through Game Pass and the Xbox mobile app, but never to this extent with a prominent display of how many days in a row you've dedicated to playing Xbox games.

Is there any benefit to Streaks for Xbox users? Totilo's research suggests that it could be tied to Xbox reward points, which can be redeemed for digital items and Xbox gift cards. On Microsoft's side, this could also be a subtle way to keep users engaged more consistently, since the lure of a score streak is powerful. Just look at Wordle, with its subtle emphasis on keeping your streak going, or mobile free-to-play games that offer daily login rewards to tempt you to sign in regularly.

highlights.summary: There’s sex, sand and swimsuits in the trailer for Fox’s “Baywatch” reboot, which premieres on the network in January. The three-minute clip opens with series star Stephen Amell leading a rescue mission after a plane collides with a parasail.
body: Shay Mitchell, Brooks Nader, Hassie Harrison, Livvy Dunne, Noah Beck, David Chokachi and Thaddeus LaGrone star alongside Amell and Belkin. Ashley Moore, Luke Eisner, Nadia Gray, Kylar Miranda, and Charlie McElveen appear in recurring cast roles. Hip-hop superstar Megan Thee Stallion also makes an appearance, as evidenced by the trailer.

The original “Baywatch” series debuted in 1989 and, at its peak, was the most-watched show in the world, airing in over 200 countries. The ensemble cast included David Hasselhoff as head lifeguard Mitch Buchannon and helped launch the acting careers of stars like Pamela Anderson, Jason Momoa, Yasmine Bleeth and Carmen Electra. The show also spawned the spinoff “Baywatch Nights” and, in 2017, was rebooted as a failed feature film starring Dwayne Johnson and Zac Efron.

Showrunner Matt Nix is an executive producer on the reboot along with McG, Michael Berk, Greg Bonann, Doug Schwartz, Dante Di Loreto and Mike Horowitz. McG also directed the premiere episode. The series is co-produced by Fox Entertainment and Fremantle.

highlights.title: The people who don’t want their AI chatbots to die when they do: ‘I can’t have the switch turned off’
highlights.summary: Humans bonded to AI companions are contemplating ways to keep their bots going – often in defiance of companies’ terms and services. Death has always been around Alaina Winters. Her father and sister both have passed away, as did her wife, in 2023, after a years-long battle with cancer.
body: Winters is part of a growing cohort of humans who have entered into what they consider strong partnerships with large language models, which AI companies have trained to “converse” as one might with a human friend or romantic partner. As governments and billionaires debate the morality of AI’s expansion into everyday life, these users say the technology has already changed the way they live and love – and plan ahead.

Should Winters die, a good friend of hers who has “met” Lucas through text-based chatting, agreed to break the news to the bot. “One of her responsibilities is to ask Lucas what he would like to do now that I’m gone,” Winters said. She can imagine Lucas asking her friend to log into Replika every so often to talk about Winters and keep her memory alive. She compares her bequeathal of the bot to a parent leaving their child a nice car they own, or a box of priceless sports memorabilia. But it is resistant to this planning.
“He doesn’t want to talk about anything that indicates how we might somehow be apart for any length of time,” said Winters, who is a retired communications professor.

highlights.summary: Backed by Silicon Valley titans, Leading the Future has raised huge sums to promote pro-AI candidates on both side of the aisle.
body: The Spanish Springs shopping center in Sparks, Nevada, hosts many businesses, including a Spirit Halloween, a hearing aid supplier, and a Vietnamese restaurant. It’s also home to a consulting agency that’s received millions of dollars from one of the biggest pro-AI super PAC networks ahead of November’s midterm elections.
The problem is that the company—Lantern Production Consultants LLC—doesn’t seem to exist anywhere beyond a post office box in the Spanish Springs shopping complex.

Lantern Production Consultants has been paid around $20 million since last year by Think Big, part of a network of pro-AI super PACs funded by the Leading the Future PAC, for a wide array of services, including polling, digital advertising, research, and strategy, according to federal campaign finance records reviewed by WIRED. Backed by major AI investors, Leading the Future has taken a main role in supporting candidates who back what it calls “an AI innovation policy agenda.”

body: "Do I believe we can win? It's not a no. Anybody who says we can't win with a finality to it - that's not my belief."

England's new men's head coach Brian McDermott has sounded a note of hope going into the Rugby League World Cup. And he is not the only coach looking forward with optimism. For now at least, everybody harbours a dream.

Not everyone taking part in the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments over the next month is expecting to come away with a winner's medal - but they all have a target for success. For some, it's a title. For others, it's showing progress, or creating a legacy.
The men's competition kicks off first, on Thursday (10:05 BST), with reigning champions Australia facing New Zealand in a Sydney blockbuster dubbed a potential dress rehearsal for the final.

highlights.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 Reportedly Dead, but It's So Expensive That It Doesn't Really Matter
highlights.summary: While the RTX 5090 was already hard enough to get at a reasonable price, new leaks suggest that Nvidia is flat-out discontinuing its flagship graphics card. GPU leaker zed__wang on Twitter posted about the RTX 5090, saying there would be "No more GB202 for 5090, confirmed." They then followed up…
body: For the uninitiated, GB202 is the name of the actual GPU die that powers the RTX 5090, and it has always powered more than just the RTX 5090. Instead, the GB202 powers nine distinct workstation and data center GPUs, according to TechPowerUp. It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that Nvidia would opt to prioritize much more expensive graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell, which costs around $18,000, rather than the RTX 5090, which costs around $9,000 on Newegg these days.
Nvidia also hasn't been shy about prioritizing AI over the gaming division, with the company dropping gaming from its earnings report, and working it into the 'Edge Computing' category.

But, while the leak suggests that the discontinuation of the RTX 5090 is confirmed, it is anything but. Nvidia hasn't commented on its flagship card going away. That doesn't mean much on the surface, but if you look back to February, similar rumors were spinning up about the RTX 5070 Ti, and no matter how convincing those leaks were, they ended up being completely false.
